Original sentence: Recent transcriptomic studies have begun to define molecular states within clinically similar disease [2-4].
Revised sentence: Recent cross-tissue transcriptomic work has identified molecular programs associated with psoriasis phenotype and severity [1].
Claim supported: PSORT cross-tissue molecular programs and phenotype/severity association.

Original sentence: single-cell/spatial studies have mapped cellular ecosystems in psoriatic tissue [5,6].
Problem: Two papers supported related but separable cellular/spatial claims.
Revised sentence: Single-cell and spatial analyses have resolved coordinated keratinocyte, fibroblast and immune-cell states in psoriatic tissue [2].
Claim supported: Psoriatic tissue cellular ecosystems and keratinocyte/fibroblast amplification.

Original sentence: Large-scale genetic studies have mapped psoriasis susceptibility and genetic sharing with inflammatory and cardiometabolic traits [1,7-10].
Problem: Cluster mixed disease overview, GWAS, PsA, CAD and Crohn claims.
Revised sentence: Large-scale GWAS has substantially expanded the inherited susceptibility map of psoriasis [3].
Action: split; remaining genetics moved to P3

Original sentence: Other transcriptomic studies have linked molecular profiles to disease severity and therapeutic response [4], while a recent Taiwanese study described a dual T helper 17/type 2 transcriptomic endotype with prominent IL-36 activation [3].
Problem: Acceptable but rewritten for clearer claim boundaries.
Revised sentence: Shrotri et al. linked transcriptomic profiles to psoriasis severity and therapeutic response [4]. Chen et al. described a dual T helper 17/type 2 transcriptomic pattern with prominent IL-36 activation in a Taiwanese psoriasis cohort [5].

Original sentence: Genetic studies have also separated aspects of psoriatic arthritis and cutaneous psoriasis architecture, identified shared psoriasis-Crohn disease loci, and reported shared genetic risk between psoriasis and coronary artery disease [8-10].
Problem: Three different genetic claims shared one cluster.
Revised sentence: Psoriatic arthritis and cutaneous psoriasis show overlapping but distinguishable genetic architectures [7]. Psoriasis also shares inherited susceptibility with coronary artery disease [8]. Earlier GWAS work identified shared susceptibility loci between psoriasis and Crohn disease [9].
Claim supported: PsA genetics, CAD shared architecture and Crohn shared loci.

Original sentence: Recent studies have reported psoriasis expression signatures associated with endotypes, disease severity, response and mixed inflammatory patterns [2-4].
Problem: Review-like cluster with multiple study-specific claims.
Revised sentence: Rider et al. demonstrated cross-tissue molecular variation associated with psoriasis phenotype and severity [1]. Shrotri et al. linked transcriptional profiles to disease severity and therapeutic response [4]. More recently, Chen et al. described a dual T helper 17/type 2 inflammatory transcriptomic phenotype in a Taiwanese cohort [5].
Claim supported: Endotype/severity, severity/response and cohort-specific inflammatory phenotype.

Original sentence: This finding is directionally consistent with previous evidence that psoriasis shares genetic risk with coronary artery disease and cardiovascular traits [8,18].
Problem: Two references supported old and newer cardiovascular genetics at different scales.
Revised sentence: Earlier cross-disease genetic analyses identified shared inherited architecture between psoriasis and coronary artery disease [8]. More recent work extended evidence of shared genetic architecture across multiple cardiovascular phenotypes [13].
Claim supported: CAD shared architecture and broader cardiovascular genetic comorbidity.

Original sentence: shared loci may act through disease-, cell-state- or stimulation-dependent regulatory effects absent from baseline GTEx tissues [15,20].
Problem: GTEx and disease-context eQTL support different concepts.
Revised sentence: GTEx provides a broad cross-tissue reference for cis-regulatory effects but primarily represents bulk reference tissue contexts [14]. Disease-context single-cell eQTL mapping has shown that regulatory effects relevant to immune-mediated disease can be restricted to specific cell types or inflammatory states [15].
Claim supported: GTEx reference scope and context-restricted eQTL.

Original sentence: A 2026 harmonized population study reported positive genetic correlations of psoriasis with Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis [19], and older shared-locus work also supports genetic overlap between psoriasis and Crohn disease [10].
Problem: Compound sentence joined genome-wide and locus-level evidence.
Revised sentence: A harmonized 2026 analysis reported positive genetic correlations between psoriasis and the major IBD subtypes [10]. At the locus level, earlier GWAS work had already identified shared susceptibility regions between psoriasis and Crohn disease [9].
Claim supported: Genome-wide IBD sharing and Crohn locus sharing.

Revised sentence: Recent organ-wide single-cell spatial mapping of human skin further shows that epithelial, stromal and immune cells are organized into multicellular neighborhoods that vary across anatomic sites and can be disrupted in disease [12].
Claim supported: Normal human skin spatial neighborhoods and disease-associated disruption.
